name: Carrion Defense Works Ricochet Pistol RCH-1 'Billiard'
description: A smart-round pistol firing self-adjusting polymer-jacketed rounds that can be programmed to ricochet off up to three surfaces before reaching a target. The weapon's integrated LiDAR maps the immediate environment and calculates bounce trajectories in real-time, displaying them on the shooter's HUD as dotted lines. The rounds contain a micro-gyroscope that adjusts the jacket's surface hardness milliseconds before each impact, controlling the angle and energy of each bounce. Carrion marketed it for engaging targets behind cover, but its real cultural impact has been in assassination — killing someone around a corner, from another room, through a ventilation duct.
specifications:
caliber: 6mm polymer-jacketed smart round
magazine: 10 rounds
maximum ricochets: 3 per round
energy retention: approximately 60% per bounce
LiDAR range: 30 meters environmental mapping
weight: 1.1 kg
trajectory calculation: 0.3 seconds per bounce path
effective kill range: 15 meters including bounces
story_hooks: A target was killed in a sealed room with no line of sight from any entry point — forensic trajectory analysis shows a triple-ricochet path through a mail slot.
The RCH-1's LiDAR mapping data is stored locally and can reconstruct a detailed 3D map of every room the weapon has been fired in — stolen units are being used as covert surveying tools.

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact, angular pistol with an almost surgical precision to its design. The frame appears almost skeletal compared to conventional firearms—lightweight polymer construction dominates, with exposed rail systems and a distinctive raised topside that houses the LiDAR module. The overall impression is of a precision instrument rather than a crude weapon; it looks like it was designed by engineers who spend more time with laser calipers than at firing ranges.
physical_description.dimensions: 18.5 cm length, 5.2 cm width at grip, 11.8 cm height including LiDAR housing. Barrel: 8.3 cm.
physical_description.weight_description: Surprisingly light in hand—the 1.1 kg weight is distributed forward toward the barrel, giving it a balanced, almost delicate feel despite the lethal engineering. Feels like holding a precision tool rather than a weapon.
physical_description.primary_material: Carbon-fiber reinforced polymer frame with brushed titanium rail systems. The LiDAR module casing appears to be aerospace-grade composite.
physical_description.finish: Satin-matte charcoal polymer with brushed titanium accents. The LiDAR housing features a subtle iridescent sheen in certain light—anti-reflective coating that hints at its sensor function.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary with silver-titanium rails and subtle teal accent lighting around the LiDAR module. Black grips with silver grip mounting points.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer grip with micro-hexagonal patterns for non-slip control. Cool to the touch, slightly rubbery. Ergonomically contoured but intentionally austere—function over comfort.
distinctive_features: Raised LiDAR module on the slide top with subtle lens elements
Dual rail systems running the length of the barrel for accessory mounting
Triangular magazine well with anti-bind geometry
Integrated status indicator LEDs (amber for low battery, teal for LiDAR lock)
Micro-texture on all contact points suggesting precision manufacturing
Visible cooling vents along the slide—likely for micro-gyroscope stabilization
Minimalist slide serrations with geometric patterns
Oversized, beveled mag release button (for gloved operation)
Custom trigger guard geometry—wider than typical pistols
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: CARRION DEFENSE WORKS stamped in all-caps along the left slide in small sans-serif font. Serial number laser-etched on the frame beneath the rail. A small circular logo (stylized carrion bird silhouette) appears on the right side of the grip. The words 'RCH-1 BILLIARD' are engraved below the manufacturer mark.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn but obsessively maintained. Light scuff marks on the polymer from tactical deployment, but no rust or significant damage. The finish shows signs of frequent field cleaning—some areas slightly dulled from repeated wiping. Micro-scratches visible under close inspection, consistent with professional use rather than abuse.
